articles.title: Astronomy for a Rainy Day
articles.summary: This article serves as a guide for amateur astronomers seeking astronomy literature in local libraries on "rainy days," when observing is not possible. It recommends a diverse collection of books covering historical observations, celestial mechanics, planetary geology, observing guides, and home observatories. The author highlights specific titles available in Cupertino and Mountain View libraries, catering to various interests and skill levels within the astronomy community.

articles.title: Observational Astronomy Classes Continue in 2000
articles.summary: SJAA member Doug Davis continues to offer free observational astronomy classes to the public at Houge Park throughout 2000. These classes provide fundamental knowledge for novices and a refresher for experienced amateurs, covering topics such as an 'Introduction to the Sky,' 'Telescopes,' and future sessions on 'Good Observing Practice,' 'Planetary Observing,' and 'Deep Sky Observing.' The program fosters interaction among participants and offers access to the SJAA Loaner Scope program.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for the month, detailing significant lunar events such as strong eastern limb libration and prime viewing of Copernicus's features. It also covers the last chances to observe giant planets Jupiter and Saturn, planetary conjunctions involving Mars, and opportunities to track asteroids Ceres and Pallas near deep-sky objects. Additionally, it briefly recounts a fascinating talk by Michael Light about his book "Full Moon."

articles.title: Meteors
articles.summary: This article offers advice on casual lunar observation, advocating for spontaneous viewing and recommending useful atlases. It also provides a detailed overview of several minor meteor showers active in March 2000, such as the Eta Virginids and Gamma Normids, along with definitions and observing notes. Complementary sections announce upcoming school star parties and a new mailing address for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: Comet Comments for March 2000
articles.summary: This article, "Comet Comments for March 2000" by Don Machholz, reports on recent comet discoveries, many found via the SOHO satellite and programs like LINEAR, Spacewatch, and Catalina. It provides detailed ephemeris and orbital elements for Comet LINEAR (C/1999 L3), which is currently brighter than predicted, and includes a note encouraging amateur astronomers to hunt for new comets in SOHO images. Many of the recently discovered comets are not expected to be visible from Earth.

articles.title: Auction XX
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting an astronomical swap meet and auction, their only fundraiser, on Saturday, April 15, at Houge Park in San Jose. The event will feature a swap meet starting at noon with a 10% seller's commission (capped at $50/item), followed by an auction at 4 PM under similar commission rules, with sellers setting minimum bids.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope Program provides astronomical telescopes for members to borrow, detailing the current status of available scopes, those on loan, and scopes with extended loan periods. Members interested in borrowing a telescope can contact Mike Koop, with options to pick up available scopes, join a waiting list, or inquire about extended loans. The article also lists various scope types and highlights a need for storage space.
